# PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS] Contents of this Part

## Coronavirus – temporary provision

## 55.A1

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.A1] (1) Practice Direction 55C makes provision for how claims under this Part (including appeals) are to proceed following the expiry of the stay provided for by rule 55.29. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.A1] (2) This Part has effect subject to Practice Direction 55C for the period specified, and in the manner specified, in Practice Direction 55C. ## Interpretation

## 55.1 In this Part –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.1 In this Part –] (a) ‘a possession claim’ means a claim for the recovery of possession of land (including buildings or parts of buildings);

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.1 In this Part –] (b) ‘a possession claim against trespassers’ means a claim for the recovery of land which the claimant alleges is occupied only by a person or persons who entered or remained on the land without the consent of a person entitled to possession of that land but does not include a claim against a tenant or sub-tenant whether his tenancy has been terminated or not;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.1 In this Part –] (c) ‘mortgage’ includes a legal or equitable mortgage and a legal or equitable charge and ‘mortgagee’ is to be interpreted accordingly;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.1 In this Part –] (d) ‘the 1985 Act’ means the Housing Act 1985 1 ; (e) ‘the 1988 Act’ means the Housing Act 1988 2 ;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.1 In this Part –] (f) ‘a demotion claim’ means a claim made by a landlord for an order under section 82A of the 1985 Act or section 6A of the 1988 Act (‘a demotion order’);

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.1 In this Part –] (g) ‘a demoted tenancy’ means a tenancy created by virtue of a demotion order; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.1 In this Part –] (h) ‘a suspension claim’ means a claim made by a landlord for an order under section 121A of the 1985 Act. ## I GENERAL RULES

## Scope

## 55.2

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (1) The procedure set out in this Section of this Part must be used where the claim includes –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (a) a possession claim brought by a –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (i) landlord (or former landlord);

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (ii) mortgagee; or

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (iii) licensor (or former licensor);

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (b) a possession claim against trespassers; or

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (c) a claim by a tenant seeking relief from forfeiture. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (Where a demotion claim or a suspension claim (or both) is made in the same claim form in which a possession claim is started, this Section of this Part applies as modified by rule 65.12. Where the claim is a demotion claim or a suspension claim only, or a suspension claim made in addition to a demotion claim, Section III of Part 65 applies). [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (2) This Section of this Part

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (a) is subject to any enactment or practice direction which sets out special provisions with regard to any particular category of claim;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (b) does not apply where the claimant uses the procedure set out in Section II of this Part; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.2] (c) does not apply where the claimant seeks an interim possession order under Section III of this Part except where the court orders otherwise or that Section so provides. ## Starting the claim

## 55.3

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.3] (1) In the County Court—

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.3] (a) the claimant may make the claim at any County Court hearing centre, unless paragraph (2) applies or an enactment provides otherwise;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.3] (b) the claim will be issued by the hearing centre where the claim is made; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.3] (c) if the claim is not made at the County Court hearing centre which serves the address where the land is situated, the claim will be sent to the hearing centre serving that address when it is issued. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.3] (Practice Direction 55A includes further direction in respect of claims which are not made at the County Court hearing centre which serves the address where the land is situated.)

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.3] (2) The claim may be started in the High Court if the claimant files with their claim form a certificate stating the reasons for bringing the claim in that court verified by a statement of truth. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.3] (3) Practice Direction 55A refers to circumstances which may justify starting the claim in the High Court. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.3] (4) Where, in a possession claim against trespassers, the claimant does not know the name of a person in occupation or possession of the land, the claim must be brought against ‘persons unknown’ in addition to any named defendants. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.3] (5) The claim form and form of defence sent with it must be in the forms set out in Practice Direction 55A. ## Particulars of claim

## 55.4 The particulars of claim must be filed and served with the claim form. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.4 The particulars of claim must be filed and served with the claim form.] (Part 16 and Practice Direction 55A provide details about the contents of the particulars of claim)

## Hearing date

## 55.5

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] (1) Subject to paragraph (1A), the court will fix a date for the hearing when it issues the claim form. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] (1A) If the claim is not made at the County Court hearing centre which serves the address where the land is situated, a date will be fixed for hearing when the claim is received by that hearing centre

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] (2) In a possession claim against trespassers the defendant must be served with the claim form, particulars of claim and any witness statements –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] (a) in the case of residential property, not less than 5 days; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] (b) in the case of other land, not less than 2 days,

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] before the hearing date. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] (3) In all other possession claims –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] (a) the hearing date will be not less than 28 days from the date of issue of the claim form;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] (b) the standard period between the issue of the claim form and the hearing will be not more than 8 weeks; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] (c) the defendant must be served with the claim form and particulars of claim not less than 21 days before the hearing date. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.5] (Rule 3.1(2)(a) provides that the court may extend or shorten the time for compliance with any rule)

## Service of claims against trespassers

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > Service of claims against trespassers] 55.6 Where, in a possession claim against trespassers, the claim has been issued against ‘persons unknown’, the claim form, particulars of claim and any witness statements must be served on those persons by –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > Service of claims against trespassers] (a)

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > Service of claims against trespassers] (i) attaching copies of the claim form, particulars of claim and any witness statements to the main door or some other part of the land so that they are clearly visible; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > Service of claims against trespassers] (ii) if practicable, inserting copies of those documents in a sealed transparent envelope addressed to ‘the occupiers’ through the letter box; or

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > Service of claims against trespassers] (b) placing stakes in the land in places where they are clearly visible and attaching to each stake copies of the claim form, particulars of claim and any witness statements in a sealed transparent envelope addressed to ‘the occupiers’. ## Defendant’s response

## 55.7

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.7] (1) An acknowledgment of service is not required and Part 10 does not apply. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.7] (2) In a possession claim against trespassers rule 15.2 does not apply and the defendant need not file a defence. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.7] (3) Where, in any other possession claim, the defendant does not file a defence within the time specified in rule 15.4, he may take part in any hearing but the court may take his failure to do so into account when deciding what order to make about costs. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.7] (4) Part 12 (default judgment) does not apply in a claim to which this Part applies. ## The hearing

## 55.8

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (1) At the hearing fixed in accordance with rule 55.5(1) or at any adjournment of that hearing, the court may –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (a) decide the claim; or

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (b) give case management directions. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (2) Where the claim is genuinely disputed on grounds which appear to be substantial, case management directions given under paragraph (1)(b) will include the allocation of the claim to a track or directions to enable it to be allocated. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (3) Except where –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (a) the claim is allocated to the fast track, the intermediate track or the multi-track; or

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (b) the court orders otherwise,

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] any fact that needs to be proved by the evidence of witnesses at a hearing referred to in paragraph (1) may be proved by evidence in writing. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (Rule 32.2(1) sets out the general rule about evidence. Rule 32.2(2) provides that rule 32.2(1) is subject to any provision to the contrary)

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (4) Subject to paragraph (5), all witness statements must be filed and served at least 2 days before the hearing. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (5) In a possession claim against trespassers all witness statements on which the claimant intends to rely must be filed and served with the claim form. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.8] (6) Where the claimant serves the claim form and particulars of claim, the claimant must produce at the hearing a certificate of service of those documents and rule 6.17(2)(a) does not apply. ## Allocation

## 55.9

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.9] (1) When the court decides the track for a possession claim, the matters to which it shall have regard include –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.9] (a) the matters set out in rule 26.13 as modified by the relevant practice direction;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.9] (b) the amount of any arrears of rent or mortgage instalments;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.9] (c) the importance to the defendant of retaining possession of the land;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.9] (d) the importance of vacant possession to the claimant; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.9] (e) if applicable, the alleged conduct of the defendant

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.9] (2) The court will only allocate possession claims to the small claims track if all the parties agree. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.9] (3) Where a possession claim has been allocated to the small claims track the claim shall be treated, for the purposes of costs, as if it were proceeding on the fast track except that trial costs shall be in the discretion of the court and shall not exceed the amount that would be recoverable under Part 45 if the value of the claim were up to £3,000. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.9] (4) Where all the parties agree the court may, when it allocates the claim, order that rule 27.14 (costs on the small claims track) applies and, where it does so, paragraph (3) does not apply. ## Possession claims relating to mortgaged residential property

## 55.10

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (1) This rule applies where a mortgagee seeks possession of land which consists of or includes residential property. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (2) Within 5 days of receiving notification of the date of the hearing by the court, the claimant must send a notice to –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (a) the property, addressed to ‘the tenant or the occupier’;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (b) the housing department of the local authority within which the property is located; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (c) any registered proprietor (other than the claimant) of a registered charge over the property. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (3) The notice referred to in paragraph (2)(a) must –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (a) state that a possession claim for the property has started;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (b) show the name and address of the claimant, the defendant and the court which issued the claim form; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (c) give details of the hearing. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (3A) The notice referred to in paragraph 2(b) must contain the information in paragraph (3) and must state the full address of the property. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (4) The claimant must produce at the hearing –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (a) a copy of the notices; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (b) evidence that they have been sent. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10] (4A) An unauthorised tenant of residential property may apply to the court for the order for possession to be suspended. ## Electronic issue of certain possession claims

## 55.10A

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (1) A practice direction may make provision for a claimant to start certain types of possession claim in certain courts by requesting the issue of a claim form electronically. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (2) The practice direction may, in particular –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (a) provide that only particular provisions apply in specific courts;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (b) specify –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (i) the type of possession claim which may be issued electronically;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (ii) the conditions that a claim must meet before it may be issued electronically;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (c) specify the court where the claim may be issued;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (d) enable the parties to make certain applications or take further steps in relation to the claim electronically;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (e) specify the requirements that must be fulfilled in relation to such applications or steps;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (f) enable the parties to correspond electronically with the court about the claim;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (g) specify the requirements that must be fulfilled in relation to electronic correspondence;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (h) provide how any fee payable on the filing of any document is to be paid where the document is filed electronically. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.10A] (3) The Practice Direction may disapply or modify these Rules as appropriate in relation to possession claims started electronically. ## II ACCELERATED POSSESSION CLAIMS OF PROPERTY LET ON AN ASSURED SHORTHOLD TENANCY

## When this section may be used

## 55.11

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.11] (1) The claimant may bring a possession claim under this Section of this Part where –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.11] (a) the claim is brought under section 21 of the 1988 Act 3 to recover possession of residential property let under an assured shorthold tenancy other than a demoted assured shorthold tenancy; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.11] (b)  all the conditions listed in rule 55.12(1) are satisfied. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.11] (2) The claim—

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.11] (a) may be brought in any County Court hearing centre; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.11] (b) will be issued by the hearing centre where it is brought. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.11] (3) In this Section of this Part, a ‘demoted assured shorthold tenancy’ means a demoted tenancy where the landlord is a registered social landlord or a private registered provider of social housing. ## Conditions

## 55.12

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.12] The conditions referred to in rule 55.11(1)(b) are that—

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.12] (a) the tenancy and any agreement for the tenancy were entered into on or after 28 February 1997;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.12] (b) the only purpose of the claim is to recover possession of the property and no other claim is made;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.12] (c) the tenancy did not immediately follow an assured tenancy which was not an assured shorthold tenancy;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.12] (d) the tenancy fulfilled the conditions provided by section 19A of the 1988 Act;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.12] (e) all the tenancies under which the defendant has occupied the property—

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.12] (i) were the subject of written agreements; or

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.12] (ii) arose by virtue of section 5 of the 1988 Act

## Claim form

## 55.13

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.13] (1) The claim form must –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.13] (a) be in the form set out in Practice Direction 55A; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.13] (b)

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.13] (i) contain such information; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.13] (ii) be accompanied by such documents,

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.13] as are required by that form. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.13] (2) All relevant sections of the form must be completed. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.13] (3) The court will serve the claim form by first class post (or an alternative service which provides for delivery on the next working day). ## Defence

## 55.14

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.14] (1) A defendant who wishes to –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.14] (a) oppose the claim; or

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.14] (b) seek a postponement of possession in accordance with rule 55.18,

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.14] must file his defence within 14 days after service of the claim form. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.14] (2) The defence should be in the form set out in Practice Direction 55A. ## Claim referred to judge

## 55.15

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] (1) On receipt of the defence the court will –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] (a) send a copy to the claimant; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] (b) refer the claim and defence to a judge. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] (2) Where the period set out in rule 55.14 has expired without the defendant filing a defence –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] (a) the claimant may file a written request for an order for possession; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] (b) the court will refer that request to a judge. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] (3) Where the defence is received after the period set out in rule 55.14 has expired but before a request is filed in accordance with paragraph (2), paragraph (1) will still apply. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] (4) Where –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] (a) the period set out in rule 55.14 has expired without the defendant filing a defence; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] (b) the claimant has not made a request for an order for possession under paragraph (2) within 3 months after the expiry of the period set out in rule 55.14,

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.15] the claim will be stayed. ## Consideration of the claim

## 55.16

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (1) After considering the claim and any defence, the judge will –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (a) make an order for possession under rule 55.17;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (b) where the judge is not satisfied as to any of the matters set out in paragraph (2) –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (i) direct that a date be fixed for a hearing; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (ii) give any appropriate case management directions; or

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (c) strike out the claim if the claim form discloses no reasonable grounds for bringing the claim. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (1A) If—

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (a) the judge directs that a date be fixed for hearing in accordance either with paragraph (2) or rule 55.18(1); and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (b) the claim has not been brought in the County Court hearing centre which serves the address where the land is situated,

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] the judge will direct that the proceedings should be transferred to that hearing centre. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (2) The matters referred to in paragraph (1)(b) are that –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (a) the claim form was served; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (b) the claimant has established that he is entitled to recover possession under section 21 of the 1988 Act against the defendant. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (3) The court will give all parties not less than 14 days’ notice of a hearing fixed under paragraph (1)(b)(i). [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (4) Where a claim is struck out under paragraph (1)(c) –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (a) the court will serve its reasons for striking out the claim with the order; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.16] (b) the claimant may apply to restore the claim within 28 days after the date the order was served on him

## Possession order

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > Possession order] 55.17 Except where rules 55.16(1)(b) or (c) apply, the judge will make an order for possession without requiring the attendance of the parties. ## Postponement of possession

## 55.18

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.18] (1) Where the defendant seeks postponement of possession on the ground of exceptional hardship under section 89 of the Housing Act 1980 6 , the judge may direct a hearing of that issue. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.18] (2) Where the judge directs a hearing under paragraph (1) –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.18] (a) the hearing must be held before the date on which possession is to be given up; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.18] (b) the judge will direct how many days’ notice the parties must be given of that hearing. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.18] (3) Where the judge is satisfied, on a hearing directed under paragraph (1), that exceptional hardship would be caused by requiring possession to be given up by the date in the order of possession, he may vary the date on which possession must be given up. ## Application to set aside or vary

## 55.19 The court may

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.19 The court may] (a) on application by a party within 14 days of service of the order; or

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.19 The court may] (b) of its own initiative,

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.19 The court may] set aside or vary any order made under rule 55.17. ## III INTERIM POSSESSION ORDERS

## When this section may be used

## 55.20

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.20] (1) This Section of this Part applies where the claimant seeks an Interim Possession Order. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.20] (2) In this section –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.20] (a) ‘IPO’ means Interim Possession Order; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.20] (b) ‘premises’ has the same meaning as in section 12 of the Criminal Law Act 1977 7 . [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.20] (3) Where this Section requires an act to be done within a specified number of hours, rule 2.8(4) does not apply. ## Conditions for IPO application

## 55.21

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.21] (1) An application for an IPO may be made where the following conditions are satisfied –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.21] (a) the only claim made is a possession claim against trespassers for the recovery of premises;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.21] (b) the claimant –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.21] (i) has an immediate right to possession of the premises; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.21] (ii) has had such a right throughout the period of alleged unlawful occupation; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.21] (c) the claim is made within 28 days of the date on which the claimant first knew, or ought reasonably to have known, that the defendant (or any of the defendants), was in occupation. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.21] (2) An application for an IPO may not be made against a defendant who entered or remained on the premises with the consent of a person who, at the time consent was given, had an immediate right to possession of the premises. ## The application

## 55.22

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (1) Rules 55.3(1) and (4) apply to the claim. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (2) The claim form and the defendant’s form of witness statement must be in the form set out in Practice Direction 55A. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (3) When he files his claim form, the claimant must also file –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (a) an application notice in the form set out in Practice Direction 55A; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (b) written evidence. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (4) The written evidence must be given –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (a) by the claimant personally; or

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (b) where the claimant is a body corporate, by a duly authorised officer. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (Rule 22.1(6)(b) provides that the statement of truth must be signed by the maker of the witness statement)

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (5) The court will –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (a) issue –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (i) the claim form; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (ii) the application for the IPO; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (b) set a date for the hearing of the application. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.22] (6) The hearing of the application will be as soon as practicable but not less than 3 days after the date of issue. ## Service

## 55.23

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.23] (1) Within 24 hours of the issue of the application, the claimant must serve on the defendant –

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.23] (a) the claim form;

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.23] (b) the application notice together with the written evidence in support; and

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.23] (c) a blank form for the defendant’s witness statement (as set out in Practice Direction 55A) which must be attached to the application notice. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.23] (2) The claimant must serve the documents listed in paragraph (1) in accordance with rule 55.6(a). [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.23] (3) At or before the hearing the claimant must file a certificate of service in relation to the documents listed in paragraph (1) and rule 6.17(2)(a) does not apply. ## Defendant’s response

## 55.24

[PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.24] (1) At any time before the hearing the defendant may file a witness statement in response to the application. [PART 55 – POSSESSION CLAIMS > 55.24] (2) The witness statement should be in the form set out in Practice Direction 55A.
